basis: Adapted from one adult inpatient psychiatry unit’s one-page procedure, version 2.0 (November 2026), written by the author. The unit, its institution and the products it uses are not named.
purpose: Every admitted patient has a documented decision about family or support-person involvement by the end of hospital day 1, and any indicated meeting is on the calendar — never improvised.
scope: Psychiatrist/APP and residents, social work, nursing, mental health technicians, unit secretary.
principle: Family work is a team workflow, not a heroic act: each step removes a handoff or a second phone call. “Family” means the people the patient chooses.

steps.title: Ask on day 1
steps.action: Ask privately: who would you want involved · what would you like them to understand · what would you rather not discuss together · what are you worried might happen. Establish consent and scope. If a joint contact is possible, the private check: “Is there anything you could not say with this person in the room?”
steps.record: Admission note: involvement decision, consent and scope
steps.doneWhen: Decision and scope documented the same day

steps.title: Collateral call = invitation
steps.action: Before dialing, check whether contact with this person by this route is safe and within the patient’s current permission. Suspected partner violence stops the joint invitation. If the call can go ahead, receive collateral. Invite the support person and record availability in the same call only if a joint meeting is safe and the patient has agreed to it. Listening is always permitted; disclose only within the documented scope.
steps.doneWhen: Family reached; availability recorded (or attempts documented)

links.label: The collateral call, step by step (Clerkship Library, written for students)

steps.title: Book it
steps.action: Enter the meeting on the shared calendar (the meeting lead’s calendar shared with the unit secretary) like any other appointment: patient, support person and phone, format and length (5-min phone update · 30-min structured · optional 60–90-min alliance repair) as set in rounds. Notify social work and the charge nurse.

steps.title: Plan in rounds
steps.action: For every patient, one line: supports · pattern · format today · who makes contact. Confirm scheduled meetings and their length. Lowest-burden format for today’s acuity; step up only as the gates are met (sleep restored, arousal down, attention holds an agenda); step down any time.
steps.record: Rounds list / family-work line in the plan
steps.doneWhen: Each patient has a format and an owner

steps.title: Bring the family up
steps.action: Meet the support person at the entrance and bring them to the unit; set up the room; let the meeting lead know they have arrived.
steps.doneWhen: Family in the room on time

steps.title: Run the meeting
steps.ownerLabel: Psychiatrist / APP / resident (+ social work or nursing when available)
steps.action: The 30 and the 60–90 share five parts: join each person · hear each experience · work on one exchange · agree what to try · close and review. Stance: PACE. A pause is available to anyone. Each participant says the task, review point, and help contact back.
steps.doneWhen: Owners, dates and contingencies agreed and repeated back

links.label: The five parts and their move cards

steps.title: Note and handoff
steps.action: See the patient alone afterwards (how it landed; new safety concerns). An ambient documentation tool drafts during the meeting → review, edit, sign. Record purpose and permission, what was worked on, what they tried, next step and who reviews, and the plan row: need · named person · date or trigger · verified · contingency. Update the support person every 72 h.
steps.doneWhen: Note signed; next owner and review point named

links.label: Check a draft against its source

steps.title: Discharge bridge
steps.action: Verify every “family will help” item: owner, date, verified, contingency. First appointment confirmed, not “being arranged.” Means-safety tasks closed and checked. A referral is not access; family willingness is not a discharge plan.
steps.doneWhen: All rows verified before the order is written

menu.name: 5-minute phone update
menu.focus: Collateral focus: baseline, no relational processing, protects fragile capacity.
menu.when: Start here when acuity is high.

menu.name: 30-minute structured meeting
menu.focus: Logistics and safety: one concrete agenda, time-bounded.
menu.when: Step up when sleep is restored (5–6 h) and arousal is down.

menu.name: 60–90-minute alliance repair (optional)
menu.focus: Relational dynamics: high expressed emotion, rupture, trauma, boundaries.
menu.when: Step up when attention holds an agenda and purpose, safety, and staffing support it.

formats.decisionRule: the lowest-burden format that matches current acuity. None, separate contacts, or deferral remain available. Document the format, why, and who reassesses.
formats.noJointMeeting: suspected partner violence · suspected family abuse · the patient declines · contact exceeds tolerance. The 5-minute phone update or separate contacts can be the plan.

guardrails: Listening is not disclosing. An involuntary status answers none of the consent questions.
No major decisions in the first 72 hours; start lower on the menu and move up when the patient can hold an agenda.
Nothing drafted by an AI tool reaches the chart or the family unreviewed; the clinician signs every line.
Describe behavior, not character, in the note; name uncertainty and discrepant accounts.
Never promise a support person that what they tell the team stays secret from the patient.

exceptions.when: Support person not reached in 24 h.
exceptions.then: Social work documents attempts and the interim plan; retry at the next rounds; patient asked for another contact.
Document; receive collateral if offered (no disclosure); revisit at 72 h and before discharge.

exceptions.when: Suspected partner violence, a positive private check, or suspected coercion.
exceptions.then: No conjoint meeting. Separate contacts or none; attending informed; safety frame, not cycle frame.
A scheduled phone or video call with the 30-minute structure counts as the meeting.
Shorten, pause, or stop; repair the alliance within 24 h; a smaller format is not a failure.

measures.cadence: Monthly, from the chart and the calendar.

list.name: % of admissions with an involvement decision documented by day 1
% of indicated meetings on the calendar within 24 h of known availability
Family meetings per day across the unit
% of discharges with every plan row verified

measures.baseline: Set the baseline for one month before setting targets.

additions.text: The sleep figure is a local pacing convention, not an evidence-derived threshold: the number is there so the team makes the same call twice.

closing: Clinical judgment, supervision, and hospital policy govern; this page describes the workflow, not the clinical decision.
